messages:
chi: FYI hit a nasty onboarding pain with `redwoodctl local-serve --container podman` on Fedora Silverblue w/ rootless podman. It fails to mount my token due to symlink permissions.
rae: same class of bug as other symlink/dotfile managers but Silverblue ostree layers make it extra weird. What's the exact error?
chi: `2026-03-05T09:41:02Z error open /root/.config/redwood/token: permission denied` from inside the container. local-serve generated the mount flag `-v /home/chi/.config/redwood:/root/.config/redwood:Z`
tom: Silverblue puts your home under an overlay, and podman rootless uses fuse-overlayfs; symlink resolution + SELinux label `Z` sometimes flips ownership to root. If the token file is a symlink, container can't follow it.
isabel: does the token live under a chezmoi-managed symlink or a drop-in from gpg/gnupg? Any special perms?
chi: chezmoi symlinked `~/.config/redwood` to `~/.local/share/chezmoi/redwood`. The token file there is `-rwxr----- 1 chi chi ... token` but the target dir is owned by root inside overlay, so container sees root-owned path.
rae: workaround for now: copy token into a plain directory in your home (e.g. `~/.redwood-plain/token`) and pass `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR=~/.redwood-plain` to local-serve. Not great for onboarding.
tom: proposal: local-serve should detect when `--container podman` is used with a symlinked config dir and, for rootless flows, offer `--mount-config=copy` which copies files into a tmpdir under $HOME and mounts that instead. Also preserve mode bits and SELinux labels with `chcon` when possible.
isabel: yes, and add a `redwoodctl doctor --mounts` check that warns about symlinked config dir + rootless podman and shows the exact mount command to reproduce. Docs should mention dotfile managers (chezmoi, stow, etc.).
chi: opened a small local patch that tries `os.Stat` and `IsSymlink` on the config dir and prints a warning. I'll open a PR with the copy-into-home fallback.
rae: can we also update quickstart onboarding to detect this during `redwoodctl init` and offer to copy token into a new path inside $HOME if we detect an overlay/symlink? That'd save a lot of fiddly support tickets.
tom: agree. Add a note in our local-serve e2e tests to run one test with a symlinked config dir to avoid regression.
dev-bot: created issue DX-1633: "local-serve (podman rootless): symlinked ~/.config/redwood leads to token permission denied; add --mount-config=copy and doctor checks" assigned to @chi, priority P2. :white_check_mark:
isabel: thanks chi — please paste minimal repro steps and the exact container logs in the issue (pid/labels if possible).
chi: will do. thanks for the quick triage :pray:
